ai.literal: Because right conduct gives excellence, right conduct must be cherished even more than life.
ai.translation: Since right conduct brings excellence, it should be guarded even more preciously than life itself.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கம் சிறப்பைத் தருவதால், அந்த ஒழுக்கத்தை உயிரை விட மேலானதாகக் கருதிப் பாதுகாக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes the supreme importance of right conduct, or decorum. The word 'viḻuppam' refers to the highest distinction, dignity, or excellence that a human can attain. Because proper conduct is the source of this greatness, the poet argues that it must be preserved at all costs. By comparing its value to 'uyir' (life) and stating it should be guarded 'uyiriṉum' (even more than life), the verse highlights that living without character is worse than death.

ai.literal: Yearningly guarding, let one protect right conduct; even if one examines and carefully investigates, that indeed is the support.
ai.translation: One should protect right conduct with great effort and care; for even if one thoroughly investigates and searches all paths, that alone is the ultimate support.
ai.modern: வருந்தியும் போற்றியும் ஒழுக்கத்தைக் காக்க வேண்டும்; ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்துத் தெளிந்தாலும், அந்த ஒழுக்கமே நமக்குச் சிறந்த துணையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of maintaining right conduct (ஒழுக்கம்). The author advises that one must protect their conduct with earnest effort (பரிந்து) and constant vigilance (ஓம்பி). Even if one thoroughly investigates and analyzes various philosophies or means of life (தெரிந்து தேரினும்), they will find that right conduct is the only true and reliable support (துணை) in life. The repetition of protective terms highlights the intense care required to preserve one's character.

ai.literal: Possessing good conduct is noble birth; misconduct will end up becoming a lowly birth.
ai.translation: Possessing good conduct constitutes true noble birth; slipping into misconduct will result in being reduced to a lowly birth.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கத்தைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே நற்குடிப் பிறப்பாகும்; ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறுதல் இழிவான பிறப்பாக முடிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet redefines nobility and lowliness based on personal character rather than ancestry. Having good conduct (oḻukkam utaimai) is what truly constitutes a noble lineage (kutimai). Conversely, slipping from moral standards (iḻukkam) degrades a person, making them equivalent to one of lowly birth (iḻinta piṟappu), regardless of their actual family background. The poet emphasizes that true status is earned through behavior, not inherited.

ai.literal: Even if forgotten, the Vedas acquiring is possible; (but) a Brahmin's birth status, when conduct slips, will be ruined.
ai.translation: Even if he forgets the Vedas, a Brahmin can learn them again; but if his right conduct slips, his very birthright of high status is ruined.
ai.modern: மறந்துபோனாலும் வேதத்தைக் கற்றுக்கொள்ள முடியும்; ஆனால், ஒரு பார்ப்பான் தன் ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறினால் அவனுடைய குடிப்பிறப்பின் உயர்வு அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of personal conduct over mere scriptural learning or birth status. The author uses the example of a Brahmin, whose traditional duty is to preserve and chant the Vedas. If such a person forgets the sacred texts, they can always be re-learned through effort. However, if he fails in his moral conduct, he loses his character, and his high birth status is instantly destroyed. Thus, character and conduct are far more fundamental and irreplaceable than rote knowledge or social lineage.

ai.literal: Like wealth with him who has envy, there is no greatness with him who lacks good conduct.
ai.translation: Just as there is no lasting prosperity in a person filled with envy, there can be no true greatness in one who lacks right conduct.
ai.modern: பொறாமை உடையவனிடத்தில் செல்வம் நிலைக்காதது போல, நல்லொழுக்கம் இல்லாதவனிடத்தில் உயர்வு இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful comparison to show that right conduct is indispensable for personal elevation. The poet states that just as wealth (ஆக்கம்) cannot truly exist or flourish in an envious person (அழுக்காறு உடையான்), true greatness (உயர்வு) cannot exist in someone who lacks proper conduct (ஒழுக்கம் இலான்). The locative suffix 'கண்' is used to denote the locus of these qualities. By linking the impossibility of wealth in the envious to the impossibility of greatness in the undisciplined, the verse highlights that moral character is the sole foundation for any real rise in life.

ai.literal: From right conduct will not waver the strong-minded ones, because of misconduct ruin befalling knowing.
ai.translation: The strong-minded will not waver from right conduct, knowing the ruin that inevitably results from slipping into misconduct.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து மனவலிமை உடையவர்கள் தளர மாட்டார்கள்; ஒழுக்கம் தவறுவதால் உண்டாகும் துன்பத்தை அவர்கள் அறிந்து வைத்திருப்பதால்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the steadfastness of wise and strong-minded individuals in maintaining right conduct. The key word 'உரவோர்' refers to those with mental strength and wisdom. They do not deviate or shrink ('ஒல்கார்') from the path of virtue ('ஒழுக்கம்') because they clearly understand ('அறிந்து') the severe ruin and suffering ('ஏதம்') that inevitably befalls ('படுபாக்கு') anyone who slips into misconduct ('இழுக்கம்'). Their adherence to virtue is not blind; it is rooted in a clear, rational comprehension of the destructive consequences of moral degradation.

ai.literal: Through good conduct they will attain greatness; through misconduct they will attain unprecedented disgrace.
ai.translation: Through right conduct, people attain greatness; through misconduct, they incur unprecedented disgrace.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கத்தினால் மக்கள் மேன்மையை அடைவார்கள்; ஒழுக்கம் தவறுதலால் அவர்கள் அடையக்கூடாத பெரும் பழியை அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the consequences of good conduct and misconduct. Those who maintain right conduct naturally rise to greatness. Conversely, those who slip into misconduct will suffer disgrace of an unprecedented or unbefitting nature. The repetition of the verb 'எய்துவர்' emphasizes that both outcomes are certain and directly earned by one's own actions. The phrase 'எய்தாப் பழி' highlights that the resulting blame is so severe that it is normally considered unthinkable.

ai.literal: To goodness a seed will become good conduct; evil conduct always misery will give.
ai.translation: Good conduct is the seed that yields virtue; evil conduct will always bring misery.
ai.modern: நல்ல ஒழுக்கம் நன்மைக்கு விதையாகும்; தீய ஒழுக்கம் எப்பொழுதும் துன்பத்தையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the long-term consequences of good and bad behavior using the metaphor of a seed. Good conduct (நல்லொழுக்கம்) is described as the seed (வித்து) that grows to produce virtue and benefit (நன்றி). In contrast, bad conduct (தீயொழுக்கம்) does not produce anything beneficial, but instead yields perpetual distress and misery (இடும்பை). The poet emphasizes that our daily behavior is the starting point for our future state of well-being or suffering.

ai.literal: To those who possess good conduct, it is impossible indeed, evil words, even by a slip of tongue, by mouth, to speak.
ai.translation: For those who possess good conduct, it is impossible to speak evil words, even by a slip of the tongue.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கம் உடையவர்களுக்கு, தவறியும் கூடத் தங்கள் வாயால் தீமையான சொற்களைச் சொல்லுதல் இயலாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how deeply good conduct is ingrained in a virtuous person. For those who possess propriety and discipline, uttering harmful or evil words is completely unnatural. Even by an accidental slip of the tongue, they will not let bad words escape their mouth. The word 'ollāvē' emphasizes that such speech is entirely incompatible with their character, showing that true conduct governs even one's involuntary utterances.

ai.literal: With the world to conform living, many things even after learning, those who have not learned are those who do not possess wisdom.
ai.translation: Those who do not know how to live in harmony with the world are ignorant, even if they have learned many vast subjects.
ai.modern: உலகத்தோடு பொருந்தி வாழக் கற்றுக் கொள்ளாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அறிவு இல்லாத கல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that practical social wisdom is far superior to mere academic learning. The phrase 'உலகத்தோடு ஒட்ட ஒழுகல்' means conducting oneself in harmony with the wise and noble people of the world. The poet asserts that even if a person has studied 'பல' (many) diverse subjects, they are still considered 'கல்லார்' (unlearned) and 'அறிவிலாதார்' (devoid of wisdom) if they lack the basic social grace to fit in with society. True education must reflect in one's behavior and ability to live peacefully among others.
